26-md01b-qb-2740.solution: A 1:20 scale means the real rocket is 20 times the model. Real height = 15 cm × 20 = 300 cm, which is 3 m.
26-md01b-qb-2740.trick: Double 15 to get 30, then add a zero to get 300 cm. That is 3 m.

26-md01b-qb-2749.solution: Taking 60° as the angle between the ladder and the ground, the height is the side opposite that angle. Height = 10 × sin 60° = 10 × (√3 ÷ 2) = 5√3 m, which is about 8.66 m.
26-md01b-qb-2749.trick: sin 60° is √3 ÷ 2, so the answer must contain √3, and only 5√3 does. Half of 10 is 5, so 5√3 it is.

26-md01b-qb-2755.trick: Do the bracket first: 2 × 2 + 2 = 6. Then 6 × 6 = 36, and 36 + 8 = 44.

26-md01b-bm-3193.solution: Each doubling multiplies the population by 2. After three doublings the population is 100 × 2³ = 100 × 8 = 800.
26-md01b-bm-3193.trick: Three doublings is the same as multiplying by 8. So 100 × 8 = 800.

26-md01b-bm-3197.solution: The integral of 2x² is 2x³/3. Between x = 0 and x = 4 it gives 2 × 4³/3 = 128/3 ≈ 42.7. The nearest option is 43 units.
26-md01b-bm-3197.trick: From x = 2 to x = 4 the curve is at least 8 high, so the area is more than 2 × 8 = 16. That rules out 9 and 12, leaving 43. As a check, the area under y = kx² from 0 is a third of the box around it, and 4 × 32 = 128, so 128 ÷ 3 ≈ 43.

26-md01b-bm-3203.solution: At 10:20 the minute hand is at 20 × 6 = 120°. The hour hand is at 10 × 30 + 20 × 0.5 = 310°. The gap is 310° − 120° = 190°, so the smaller angle is 360° − 190° = 170°.
26-md01b-bm-3203.trick: With the hour hand on the 10 and the minute hand on the 4, the hands are 180° apart. At 10:20 the hour hand has crept 10° past the 10 (20 × 0.5°), which shrinks the short gap to 180° − 10° = 170°.

26-md01b-bm-3209.solution: In Hardy Weinberg equilibrium the heterozygote frequency is 2pq. With q = 0.3, p = 1 − 0.3 = 0.7. So 2pq = 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42.
26-md01b-bm-3209.trick: Heterozygotes are 2pq: 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.21, then double it to get 0.42. The 0.21 option forgets the 2, and 0.09 is q².

26-md01b-bm-3219.solution: Factorise: v = t² − 6t + 8 = (t − 2)(t − 4), so v = 0 at t = 2 and t = 4. At t = 3, v = 9 − 18 + 8 = −1, which is negative. The parabola opens upwards, so v is negative only between the roots: 2 < t < 4.
26-md01b-bm-3219.trick: The roots add up to 6 and multiply to 8, so they are 2 and 4. An upward parabola is negative between its roots.

26-md01b-bm-3225.solution: Diluting the stock 5 times divides its concentration by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 mg/mL. Volume = dose ÷ concentration = 25 mg ÷ 2 mg/mL = 12.5 mL.
26-md01b-bm-3225.trick: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 mg/mL. Then 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5, which is half of 25.

26-md01b-bm-3231.solution: Four tosses give 2⁴ = 16 equally likely outcomes. Only TTTT has no head. So P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/16 = 15/16.
26-md01b-bm-3231.trick: Use the complement. Only all tails fails, which is 1 in 16, so the answer is 15/16.

26-md01b-bm-3235.solution: 12 km = 12,000 m and 1 litre = 1,000 mL. So 12 km per litre = 12,000 m per 1,000 mL = 12 m/mL.
26-md01b-bm-3235.trick: The 1,000 in km to m cancels the 1,000 in L to mL, so the number stays 12.

26-md01b-bm-3239.solution: Using h = 4 means the difference quotient (f(2 + h) − f(2)) ÷ h, not the exact derivative (which would be 2x = 4 at x = 2). Here f(6) = 36 and f(2) = 4. So the answer is (36 − 4) ÷ 4 = 32 ÷ 4 = 8.
26-md01b-bm-3239.trick: For x², the difference quotient simplifies to 2x + h, which is 4 + 4 = 8.

26-md01b-bm-3245.solution: Multiply matching components and add. A · B = 3 × 4 + (−2) × 1 = 12 − 2 = 10.
26-md01b-bm-3245.trick: First parts: 3 × 4 = 12. Second parts: (−2) × 1 = −2. Add them to get 10.

26-md01b-bm-3253.solution: The show counts each magnitude step as 10 times more energy, so 10⁶ times the energy is 6 steps up from 4: 4 + 6 = 10. In real seismology each step is about 32 times the energy (10 to the power 1.5), so 10⁶ is 6 ÷ 1.5 = 4 steps and the magnitude would be 8. But 8 is not among the options. So the show's answer is 10.
26-md01b-bm-3253.trick: On the show's rule, the exponent 6 is the number of steps, so add it to 4 to get 10. Real Richter steps are worth 1.5 powers of ten each, so the real answer is 4 + 6 ÷ 1.5 = 8.

26-md01b-bm-3262.solution: Doubling every 30 minutes means the count is multiplied by 2 in each period, so time sits in the exponent. A linear function adds the same amount each time, and a logarithmic function grows ever more slowly. So the best model is an exponential function.
26-md01b-bm-3262.trick: Doubling means repeated multiplying, and repeated multiplying is exponential. Linear adds a fixed amount and logarithmic slows down, so neither fits doubling.

26-md01b-bm-3268.solution: A 1:500 scale means the real building is 500 times the model. Actual height = 8 cm × 500 = 4,000 cm. Divide by 100 to change to metres: 40 m.
26-md01b-bm-3268.trick: At 1:500, 1 cm on the model is 500 cm, which is 5 m. So 8 cm is 8 × 5 = 40 m.

26-md01b-bm-3272.trick: 88 − 75 = 13. Shift the decimal point one place to get 1.3.

26-md12a-qb-0507.solution: Magnification = image size ÷ object size, so object size = image size ÷ magnification. That is 8 mm ÷ 1,600 = 0.005 mm.

26-md12a-qb-0514.solution: The firework is back on the ground when h = 0. So −16t² + 192t = 0, which factorises as −16t(t − 12) = 0. The roots are t = 0 (the launch) and t = 12, so it lands after 12 seconds.
26-md12a-qb-0514.trick: The landing time is the t coefficient over the t² coefficient: 192 ÷ 16 = 12.

26-md12a-qb-0551.solution: Percentage = part ÷ whole × 100. So it is 25 mL ÷ 500 mL × 100 = 5%.
26-md12a-qb-0551.trick: 25 out of 500 is 5 out of 100, so 5%.

26-md12a-qb-0586.solution: Energy = power × time, so change the time to seconds first: 6 h × 3,600 = 21,600 s. E = 100 W × 21,600 s = 2,160,000 J. Divide by 1,000 to get kilojoules: 2,160 kJ.
26-md12a-qb-0586.trick: 100 W is 0.1 kJ per second, so take a tenth of the seconds: 21,600 ÷ 10 = 2,160 kJ.

26-md12a-qb-0593.solution: Percentage saved = saved ÷ earned × 100 = 70,000 ÷ 500,000 × 100. Cancel the zeros: 7 ÷ 50 × 100 = 14%.
26-md12a-qb-0593.trick: 70,000 out of 500,000 cancels to 7 out of 50. Double both to get 14 out of 100, so 14%.

26-md12a-qb-0620.solution: Profit = revenue − expenses = 80,000 − 60,000 = 20,000. Profit margin = profit ÷ revenue × 100 = 20,000 ÷ 80,000 × 100 = 25%.
26-md12a-qb-0620.trick: Profit is 20 out of 80, which is one quarter, so 25%.

26-md12a-qb-0623.solution: A square has 4 equal sides, so perimeter = 4 × side. Side = 160 m ÷ 4 = 40 m.
26-md12a-qb-0623.trick: Half of 160 is 80, and half again is 40.

26-md12a-qb-0638.solution: Assuming Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, the AA genotype frequency is p². With p = 0.7, p² = 0.7 × 0.7 = 0.49.
26-md12a-qb-0638.trick: Square the 7: 7 × 7 = 49. Two decimal places gives 0.49.

26-md12a-qb-0646.solution: Power = energy ÷ time, with time in seconds. 4 minutes = 4 × 60 = 240 s. So P = 20 J ÷ 240 s = 1/12 W.
26-md12a-qb-0646.trick: 4 minutes is 240 seconds. 20 ÷ 240 cancels to 2 ÷ 24, which is 1/12.

26-md12a-qb-0660.solution: The population grows by a factor of 8,000 ÷ 1,000 = 8. Since 8 = 2³, that is 3 doublings. At 2 hours per doubling, the time is 3 × 2 = 6 hours.
26-md12a-qb-0660.trick: Count the doublings: 1,000, 2,000, 4,000, 8,000 is 3 steps. Then 3 × 2 hours = 6 hours.

26-md12a-qb-0663.solution: The resultant is the vector sum, added component by component. The i parts give 5 + (−3) = 2 and the j parts give 2 + 4 = 6. So the resultant is 2i + 6j.
26-md12a-qb-0663.trick: Add the i parts (5 − 3 = 2) and the j parts (2 + 4 = 6) separately.

26-md12a-qb-0671.solution: Simple interest = principal × rate × time = 10,000 × 0.02 × 1 = 200. Balance = 10,000 + 200 = $10,200.
26-md12a-qb-0671.trick: 2% of 10,000 is 200 (1% is 100, so double it). Add it on to get $10,200.

26-md12a-qb-0677.solution: Work = force × distance moved in the direction of the force. W = 12 N × 5 m = 60 J.
26-md12a-qb-0677.trick: Multiply directly: 12 × 5 is half of 120, which is 60.
